title: Connector relay: WebSocket streams
description: WebSocket open, data and close frames per chat, derived from the portal's two-socket relay (web-chat-dev.worktrees/ae-int/lib/portal/ws-relay.js createWsRelay, whose upstream half moves to the shared lib/relay with early and pause/resume, contract 05 section 4: the viewer's handshake completes only once the upstream is open, the upstream opens with no Origin and with X-WC-Remote, close codes 4401, 4403, 4503; identical on web-chat-dev main). A message travels as one or more relay.ws.data fragments (C-05.23). Flow control is relay.window in 05-relay-http.json.

open.description: Open the chat's live surface socket (C-05.34). Only the session surface has one, at /ws. Direction: hub to connector.

ch.description: The channel this frame travels on (C-05.10).

kind.description: The frame kind within its channel.

id.description: This frame's id, unique per sender per connection. A reply names it in `re`.

seq.description: Per connection, per channel, per direction: 1 for the first frame, plus 1 for each next (C-05.11). Durable positions live in the bodies (contract 07 cursors, hub_msg_id, contract 06 rev), never here.

at.description: When the sender built the frame. Informative; never used for ordering or expiry.

stream.description: The relay stream, minted by the hub, unique per connection. One HTTP exchange or one WebSocket is one stream.

chat.description: The chat label (contract 03 section 2): the chat id without its `cht_` prefix, 26 lowercase Crockford base32 characters, so that `chat-<label>.<hub>` and `chat-<label>-a.<hub>` are literal. Every 05 frame and every 06 body names a chat by its label; the hub records the id.

path.description: The only socket a daemon serves (lib/server/ws.js).

user_agent.description: The viewer's User-Agent, the one handshake header lib/portal/ws-relay.js forwards (push provenance).

actor.description: The X-WC-Actor value for this request, built by the hub and copied verbatim by the connector (contract 03, C-03.19 to C-03.21). The connector never builds, alters or reuses one.

decision.description: The current policy decision for this principal on this chat (contract 04, C-04.8). The connector stamps X-WC-Level, X-WC-Grants and X-WC-Decision from it and gates the route with it.

decision_ref.description: Instead of `decision`: a decision the hub already sent on this connection in a relay.decision frame (C-05.31).

device.description: The viewer's device class as the hub saw it. Informative: the daemon's own push provenance comes from the request (lib/server/domain/queue.js provenance).

opened.description: The upstream socket to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws is open; the hub completes the viewer's handshake now, not before (C-05.34). Direction: connector to hub.

refused.description: The upstream would not open (C-05.34). The hub answers the viewer's handshake with this status and body, as refuseUpgrade does. Direction: connector to hub.

status.description: 403 the connector's gate refused it; 404 the chat is not running here; 429 too many streams; 502 the daemon did not answer or refused; 503 the hub is failing closed or the chat is restricted (contract 12 read_only_relay does not refuse reads). Pause never refuses a relay (C-05.27).

anyOf.description: The portal's refusal shape for anything but a policy refusal (lib/portal/ws-relay.js refuseUpgrade bodies, lib/portal/index.js NOT_ANSWERING).

remote.description: Answered by the relay, not the page.

error.description: In the portal's words, for example: this session's daemon is not answering.

data.description: One fragment of one WebSocket message, either direction (C-05.23, C-05.35). A message is sent as one or more of these, at most 262144 bytes decoded each, all but the last with more: true; the receiver reassembles before it writes. Text stays text (split only at code point boundaries), binary stays binary. The sender measures the encoded frame, never the message, against C-05.10's 1 MiB. Direction: both directions.

binary.description: False: `data` is text, a piece of the text message. True: `data` is standard base64 of a piece of the binary message. The same on every fragment of one message.

more.description: True: more fragments of this message follow on this stream. Absent or false: this fragment ends the message (C-05.23).

data.description: This fragment: at most 262144 bytes decoded (UTF-8 bytes for text). A whole message daemon to viewer is at most 100 MiB (the daemon's own ws limit), larger closes the stream with 1009; viewer to daemon, contract 04 C-04.18's 1 MiB inbound cap holds, applied by the connector to the reassembled message before it is sent to the daemon (C-05.23).

close.description: Close a socket stream, either direction (C-05.36). A close on either side closes the other, as ws-relay.js does; the connector closes the daemon socket within 1 s. Direction: both directions.

code.description: A WebSocket close code: the daemon's or the viewer's, passed through (new against ws-relay.js:162-164, which closes the other side with no code), or one the hub or connector cuts with (C-05.36), 1009 for a message over C-05.23's bound.

reason.description: The close reason (123 bytes is the WebSocket limit).
